name: Morocco
genZNote: Morocco sits just 14 km from Europe across the Strait of Gibraltar — close enough that on a clear day you can see Spain from its coast — making it the classic geography-exam example of two continents almost, but not quite, touching.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Located in northwestern Africa (the Maghreb region), bordered by Algeria and the Western Sahara territory, with coastlines on both the Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea.
Separated from Spain by only the narrow Strait of Gibraltar (about 14 km at its narrowest point) at its northern tip.
Diverse terrain including the Atlas Mountains, the Sahara Desert in the south, and fertile agricultural plains along the Atlantic coast.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Arabic and Berber (Tamazight) are both official languages, reflecting Morocco's deep indigenous Amazigh (Berber) heritage alongside Arab influence; French remains widely used in business and education.
A predominantly Muslim country with a rich architectural and artistic heritage blending Arab, Berber, Andalusian, and French colonial influences.
Famous for its historic walled cities (medinas), including Fez and Marrakech, and traditional crafts like carpet weaving and leatherwork.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A constitutional monarchy where the King holds significant executive powers alongside an elected Prime Minister and bicameral Parliament.
The Alaouite dynasty has ruled Morocco since the 17th century, giving it one of the longest-reigning royal families in the world.
Gained independence from French and Spanish colonial rule in 1956, though the disputed status of Western Sahara remains an unresolved territorial issue.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A growing regional hub for renewable energy, particularly the Noor Ouarzazate Solar Complex, one of the world's largest concentrated solar power plants.
Developing automotive and aerospace manufacturing sectors, positioning Morocco as an increasingly significant industrial hub for Africa and Europe.
Strong phosphate mining and processing industry, given Morocco's position holding a large share of the world's known phosphate reserves (essential for fertiliser production).

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A key African and Arab world diplomatic bridge, rejoining the African Union in 2017 after decades of absence over the Western Sahara dispute.
Maintains close historical and economic ties with France and Spain, given colonial-era history and geographic proximity.
Joined the 2020 Abraham Accords, normalising relations with Israel alongside several other Arab states.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Morocco maintain warm relations, with Morocco being a critical supplier of phosphates and phosphoric acid, essential raw materials for India's fertiliser industry.
Growing cooperation in agriculture, renewable energy, and pharmaceuticals.
Morocco has historically supported India's position on several international issues, and the two countries maintain regular high-level diplomatic engagement.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: Holds a very large share of the world's known phosphate reserves, a critical raw material for global fertiliser production.
A growing manufacturing hub for automobiles and aerospace components, alongside a robust tourism and textile export sector.
A regional leader in renewable energy, particularly large-scale solar power projects.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Historic walled cities (medinas) of Fez and Marrakech.
Holding a dominant share of the world's phosphate reserves.
The Noor Ouarzazate Solar Complex, one of the world's largest solar power plants.
Being a key gateway between Africa, Europe, and the Arab world.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Moroccan Dirham (MAD).
A diversified economy with strengths in agriculture, phosphate mining (holding the world's largest reserves), automotive manufacturing, and tourism.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Spans the Atlas Mountains, Mediterranean coast, and the edge of the Sahara Desert.
Home to unique argan forests (a UNESCO biosphere reserve), source of the globally exported argan oil.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Home to ancient Berber (Amazigh) civilizations and later Arab-Islamic dynasties.
Became a French and Spanish protectorate in the early 20th century; regained independence in 1956.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1956 independence from France and Spain.
A constitutional monarchy; the 2011 Constitution, adopted amid the Arab Spring, expanded the powers of the elected government relative to the monarchy.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: Moroccan Royal Centre for Remote Sensing supports satellite and space-research activity.
A regional leader in renewable energy, notably the Noor Ouarzazate solar power complex, one of the world's largest concentrated solar plants.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Football achieved historic success, becoming the first African and Arab team to reach a FIFA World Cup semi-final (2022).
The medina of Fez and the city of Marrakech are UNESCO World Heritage Sites renowned for their architecture and craftsmanship.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Member of the UN, the Arab League, and the African Union (which it rejoined in 2017).
Maintains close economic and political ties with the European Union.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Morocco is a constitutional monarchy in northwestern Africa, close to Europe via the Strait of Gibraltar, and a critical global supplier of phosphates for fertiliser.
keyFacts: Constitutional monarchy; Alaouite dynasty has ruled since the 17th century.
Holds a dominant share of the world's known phosphate reserves.
Home to one of the world's largest solar power plants (Noor Ouarzazate).
commonConfusion: Morocco's largest city is Casablanca, but its capital is Rabat — a common point of confusion.

highYieldFacts: Morocco: constitutional monarchy, capital Rabat, Alaouite dynasty since the 17th century.
Dominant global phosphate reserve holder — critical for fertiliser production.
India-Morocco: key phosphate/phosphoric acid supplier for India's fertiliser industry.
commonTraps: Assuming Casablanca is Morocco's capital — it is Rabat.
Overlooking the unresolved Western Sahara territorial dispute when discussing Morocco's borders.
mustRemember: Morocco: constitutional monarchy, top phosphate supplier for India's fertiliser sector, major solar-energy investor, Africa-Europe-Arab bridge.
